title: The Psychology of Procrastination
instructions: For questions 1-8, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals at the end of each line to form a word that fits in the gap in the same line.
passage:
Procrastination is often (1)___ as a simple failure of willpower, but psychologists increasingly argue that it is far more (2)___ than that.

Far from being driven purely by laziness, chronic procrastinators are frequently highly (3)___ individuals who delay tasks precisely because they care so much about doing them well. The fear of producing (4)___ work, rather than indifference, can be what triggers the (5)___ to begin.

This (6)___ to start is rarely a conscious choice; it is better understood as an automatic, almost (7)___ response to the discomfort that a difficult task provokes. Treating it as a moral failing, researchers warn, tends to increase shame without improving (8)___, and may even make the underlying avoidance worse.

questions.explanation: The prefix 'mis-' gives 'misunderstood' (= wrongly interpreted), which fits the idea that procrastination is wrongly seen as just a lack of willpower.
The adjective form 'complicated' fits after 'far more ___ than that'.
'Conscientious' (= careful and diligent) fits people who delay tasks because they care deeply about doing them well.
The negative prefix 'im-' gives 'imperfect', fitting the fear of producing work that isn't good enough.
The noun form 'reluctance' is needed after 'the' and before 'to begin'.
The noun 'hesitation' fits as the subject of the sentence ('This hesitation to start...').
The adjective 'reflexive' (= automatic, done without thinking) fits 'an almost ___ response'.
